original_value: To address the issues encountered when using traditional airplane detection methods, including the low accuracy rate, high false alarm rate, and low detection speed due to small object sizes in aerial remote sensing images, we propose a remote sensing image airplane detection method that uses multilayer feature fusion in fully convolutional neural networks. The shallow layer and deep layer features are fused at the same scale after sampling to overcome the problems of low dimensionality in the deep layer and the inadequate expression of small objects. The sizes of candidate regions are modified to fit the size of the actual airplanes in the remote sensing images. The fully connected layers are replaced with convolutional layers to reduce the network parameters and adapt to different input image sizes. The region proposal network shares convolutional layers with the detection network, which ensures high detection efficiency. The simulation results indicate that, when compared to typical airplane detection methods, the proposed method is more accurate and has a lower false alarm rate. Additionally, the detection speed is considerably faster and the method can accurately and rapidly complete airplane detection tasks in aerial remote sensing images.

result.paraphrase: To overcome the shortcomings of traditional airplane detection methods—such as low accuracy, a high false-alarm rate, and slow detection caused by the small size of objects in aerial remote sensing images—we present an airplane detection approach for remote sensing images based on multilayer feature fusion in fully convolutional neural networks. After sampling, shallow and deep features are fused at the same scale to address the low dimensionality of deep-layer features and the insufficient representation of small objects. Candidate region sizes are adjusted to match the actual airplane sizes in remote sensing images. Fully connected layers are replaced by convolutional layers to reduce network parameters and support varying input image sizes. The region proposal network shares convolutional layers with the detection network, ensuring efficient detection. Simulation results show that, compared with conventional airplane detection methods, the proposed approach is more accurate and has a lower false-alarm rate. It is also significantly faster and can accurately and rapidly perform airplane detection in aerial remote sensing images.
